study_type_evidence.quote: 200 μL Sulforhodamine 101 acid chloride-labelled AuNp-DPA (2 mg/kg) were administered by intravenous injection via tail vein.
Tumor cells (HCT116 p53+/+, 4×106 cells/site) were injected subcutaneously into BALB/c nude mice with four to five weeks old.
Targeted tumor enrichment ability of AuNP-DPA ex vivo.
AuNp-PDA was very easily soluble in water and maintained monodispersity after 24 h incubation in 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS) in PBS buffer at pH 7.4
HCT116 cells were first cultured for 24 h. The medium was then replaced with the medium containing AuNp-DPAFITC
To test GSH-responsive drug release, AuNP-DPA were dissolved in PBS buffer (pH 7.4) containing 10 mM GSH

in_vivo_species.strain_sex_age: athymic BALB/c nude, four to five weeks old at tumour implantation; sex not reported
in_vivo_species.quote: Tumor cells (HCT116 p53+/+, 4×106 cells/site) were injected subcutaneously into BALB/c nude mice with four to five weeks old.

ex_vivo_detail: Two ex vivo elements. (1) Serum-containing stability assay: AuNP-DPA was incubated for 24 h in 10% fetal bovine serum in PBS pH 7.4 and monodispersity was confirmed by dynamic light scattering (bovine serum). (2) Ex vivo biodistribution: BALB/c nude mice bearing HCT116 xenografts were sacrificed 6 h after intravenous or intraperitoneal dosing, organs and tumours were excised and imaged on the IVIS Spectrum System (λex 590 nm; λem 610 nm), and fluorescence was semi-quantified with Living Image 3.0 (Figure 6A-F). Harvested tumour and organ tissues were also processed for H&E, TUNEL and immunohistochemistry.
in_vitro_detail: Cell culture: HCT116 p53+/+ and HCT116 p53-/- colon cancer cells (uptake by confocal microscopy and flow cytometry, apoptosis by Annexin V-PI, cell cycle, western blot for p53/p21); normal cells and p53-null SW480 for cytotoxicity. Cell-free: GSH-responsive release of DPA-Cys from AuNP-DPA in PBS pH 7.4 ± 10 mM GSH monitored by HPLC and ESI-MS; drug loading quantified in 6 M GuHCl / 1 M DTT by HPLC. Uptake-pathway blockade with free RGDDP (50 μM), amiloride (3 mM) and cytochalasin D (2 μM).

agents.name: AuNP-DPA (ultra-small gold nanoparticle core conjugated with DPA-Cys, coated with polylysine and surface-modified with the RGD-derived peptide RGDDP)
agents.sequence: DPA payload: TAWYANFEALLR (D-peptide p53 activator); conjugated as DPA-Cys: TAWYANFEALLRC, with the N-terminal amino group acetylated. Targeting peptide RGDDP is given inconsistently in the body as CRGDKRGDSP (Introduction) and RGDSPRGDR (Results).
agents.sequence_source: Results, "Synthesis and characterization of AuNP-DPA": "an extra cysteine was added to the C terminus of DPA (DPA-Cys: TAWYANFEALLRC; Figure S2A)"; Introduction gives "D-peptide p53 activator DPA (TAWYANFEALLR)"
agents.chemical_identifier: Au core from HAuCl4·xH2O (Aladdin Chemicals) by the HEPES method; ~4 nm TEM core diameter, ~5 nm hydrated size (PDI 0.02); polylysine MW 1500-2000; DPA-Cys loading 0.5 mmol/g; RGDDP coupled via N-succinimidyl maleimidoacetate; peptides from CS Bio (Shanghai)
agents.group_n: PK/circulation study: n = 3 at each time point. Efficacy study: five mice per group (25 mice across five groups).
agents.group_n_quote: blood samples were collected from the retro-orbital sinus of anesthetized mice at indicated time points (n=3 at each time points)
agents.dose: 2 mg/kg (200 μL) single dose for the circulation-time and biodistribution studies; 2 mg/kg every other day on days 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 and 11 for the 13-day efficacy study
agents.route: intravenous via tail vein for the PK/circulation study; intraperitoneal for the efficacy study (biodistribution assessed after both iv and ip)
agents.dose_route_quote: 200 μL Sulforhodamine 101 acid chloride-labelled AuNp-DPA (2 mg/kg) were administered by intravenous injection via tail vein.
agents.half_life_matrix: mouse blood (whole-blood samples from the retro-orbital sinus of athymic BALB/c nude mice, quantified by sulforhodamine 101 fluorescence)
agents.pk_quote: the nanoparticle presented a long half-life of 7.5 h with a first order elimination rate (Figure S13)

concentration_time_figure.locator: Figure S13 (supplementary) for the in vivo blood circulation curve; Figure 4E for in vitro cumulative release versus time
concentration_time_figure.caption_quote: the nanoparticle presented a long half-life of 7.5 h with a first order elimination rate (Figure S13)
concentration_time_figure.note: Figure S13 is cited in the body as the source of the in vivo blood circulation-time data from which the 7.5 h first-order half-life was derived; the figure itself is supplementary and its caption is not reproduced in the body text, so the exact axes could not be confirmed. Figure 4E plots cumulative DPA-Cys release from AuNP-DPA versus time in 10 mM GSH/PBS (~50% at ~0.6 h, ~100% by 2 h) - an in vitro release profile, not an in vivo concentration-time curve.

bioanalytical_method: For the in vivo circulation-time study: fluorescence of sulforhodamine 101 acid chloride (Texas Red-X)-labelled AuNP-DPA in heparinised blood, read on a microplate reader (λex 586 nm; λem 605 nm) against a standard curve prepared in blood from PBS-treated mice. Biodistribution used IVIS Spectrum fluorescence imaging (λex 590 nm; λem 610 nm). HPLC (with ESI-MS confirmation) was used for drug loading and GSH-triggered release in vitro.
bioanalytical_quote: The blood samples were determined using a microplate reader (λex 586 nm; λem 605 nm).
notes: The 7.5 h half-life is reported in the body without an error term (the '± 0.8' in the peplife2 metadata block does not appear in the body and was not used). The PK assay was fluorescence of the sulforhodamine-101 label on a microplate reader, NOT HPLC as the peplife2 metadata states; HPLC was used only for in vitro drug loading and GSH-triggered release. The PK/circulation study dosed intravenously via tail vein at 2 mg/kg, whereas the efficacy study used intraperitoneal dosing; the authors state there was no difference in biodistribution between routes (Figure S14). Sex of the BALB/c nude mice is not reported. The RGDDP targeting peptide sequence is given inconsistently in the body: 'CRGDKRGDSP' in the Introduction versus 'RGDSPRGDR' in the Results; the Results also describes RGDDP as consisting of the motifs RGDK and RGDSP. The efficacy Methods state 'AuNP-DPA, AuNP and DPA wre administered at dose of 2 mg/kg', while the Figure 7A caption lists '2 mg/kg DPA, 2 mg/kg AuNP-DPA or 2 mg/kg AuNP' and '1.5 mg/kg doxorubicin'. No Cmax, Tmax, AUC, clearance or volume of distribution values are reported anywhere in the body.
